National News Bihar Congress plans phased agitation over voter rights until November, demands CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation By: Sunita Sarkar Date: October 9, 2026 Patna, Oct 9 (IANS) The Bihar Congress has announced a phased agitation through November to highlight concerns over voter rights and complaints about names of genuine voters being deleted from electoral rolls. The party will also demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar as part of its campaign. Under the programme, Congress workers will organise marches at block headquarters from October 10 to 20, followed by village-level ‘Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao (Save Vote, Save Country)’ chaupals from October 25 to November 25. The final phase will involve a proposed ‘Delhi Chalo’ march on Constitution Day, with thousands of party workers expected to participate in the stir over voter rights. The agitation strategy was discussed at a review meeting held on Friday at Sadaqat Ashram in Patna. Bihar Congress in-charge Krishna Allavaru and State President Rajesh Ram attended the meeting along with district presidents and state office-bearers. Participants reviewed the organisation’s current status, ongoing public outreach initiatives and preparations for upcoming programmes. The leadership stressed the need to expand the campaign to block, panchayat and village levels and increase participation among party workers. Krishna Allavaru called for strengthening the organisation at the booth, panchayat and block levels. He urged district presidents and office-bearers to implement party programmes effectively and maintain regular communication with the public. He also emphasised better coordination across different levels of the organisation. The first phase of the agitation will run from October 10 to 20, with marches planned at block headquarters. The demonstrations will focus on voter rights and complaints from people who claim their names have been removed from the electoral rolls. State President Rajesh Ram said the campaign would bring the grievances of affected voters to the forefront and raise public awareness about the issue. The party intends to use the protests to draw attention to difficulties faced by people who say they have been excluded from voter lists. In the second phase, Congress workers will organise ‘Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’ chaupals in villages between October 25 and November 25. The meetings will provide a platform for people to raise concerns about alleged deletions from electoral rolls. Party workers will engage with affected individuals, listen to their complaints and spread awareness about voting rights. The Congress plans to expand the campaign at the grassroots level to encourage wider public participation and strengthen its voter outreach. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Bullet Train Project: Patna Selected Among 5 Proposed Stations - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next Bihar Bullet Train Project: Patna Selected Among 5 Proposed Stations 09 Oct 2026 2 min read Why in News? Bihar is set to become an important part of India’s expanding high-speed rail network, with the proposed Varanasi-Patna-Siliguri high-speed rail corridor expected to improve connectivity across the state. The project is expected to leverage Japanese Shinkansen technology , renowned for its high speed, safety and operational efficiency. Key Points Announcement of High-Speed Rail Corridors: The Union Budget 2026-27 announced seven new high-speed rail corridors, including Delhi-Varanasi and Varanasi via Patna to Siliguri. According to reports on the proposed Bihar alignment, five districts have been identified for bullet train stations. These include Patna, Buxar, Begusarai, Khagaria and Katihar. Potential Economic Benefits For Bihar: A high-speed rail connection could boost Bihar’s economic growth. Improved connectivity could promote business, tourism, investment, logistics and employment generation around major stations. Japanese Shinkansen Technology The Shinkansen is Japan’s high-speed railway network, famously known as the Bullet Train . It began operations in 1964 on the Tokaido line connecting Tokyo and Osaka. It relies on advanced technology, strict safety standards, specialised maintenance and operational discipline. The Mumbai–Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail Corridor is India’s first bullet train project, developed with Japan’s technical and financial cooperation using Shinkansen technology. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Plans ₹1.88 Lakh Crore Energy Investment - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next Bihar Plans ₹1.88 Lakh Crore Energy Investment 09 Oct 2026 2 min read Why in News? Bihar has proposed ₹1.88 lakh crore in energy-sector investments , covering power generation, storage, transmission, distribution and renewable energy. The state aims to achieve 24 GW of renewable energy capacity and 6.1 GWh of energy storage capacity by 2029–30 . Key Points Energy Investment and Demand: Bihar has proposed ₹1,88,383 crore in energy-sector investments; peak electricity demand is projected to reach 11,747 MW by 2030 . Power Generation and Storage: Around ₹1,32,521 crore is proposed for generation and storage, including 8,400 MW of pumped storage across four districts and a 150 MW solar park in Aurangabad. A 2,800 MW nuclear power project is proposed in Banka. Renewable Energy: Bihar targets 24 GW of renewable energy and 6.1 GWh of energy storage by 2029–30 . Plans include 1,100 MW of rooftop solar for Kutir Jyoti consumers and 500 MW on government buildings. Green Hydrogen: An outlay of around ₹1,040 crore is planned for green hydrogen development, including five pilot Green Hydrogen Villages , with ₹1 crore per selected village. Transmission and Distribution: Proposed investments include ₹24,683 crore for transmission , ₹28,809 crore for distribution and ₹2,370 crore for maintenance and digital infrastructure, building upon Bihar Policy for Promotion of New and Renewable Energy Sources, 2025. Bihar Policy for Promotion of New and Renewable Energy Sources, 2025 Objective: Promote renewable energy development, attract investment, and strengthen Bihar’s energy security. Renewable Energy Expansion: Encourage solar, wind, biomass, small hydro, and other clean-energy projects. Investment and Incentives: Provide policy support and incentives to encourage private-sector participation in renewable energy development. Energy Storage: Promote battery and pumped-storage systems to improve grid stability and support renewable energy integration. Green Energy Transition: Support the adoption of cleaner energy technologies, reduce dependence on conventional energy sources, and promote sustainable development. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary Sets Target Of Making 1 Crore Families Self-Reliant Through ...
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary Sets Target Of Making 1 Crore Families Self-Reliant Through Entrepreneurship Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary launched the MSME Policy 2026, targeting one crore families for self-reliance through entrepreneurship. The state plans to develop 45,000 entrepreneurs with an outlay of Rs 3,500 crore, attract Rs 5 lakh crore in industrial investment and encourage youth to become job creators rather than job seekers. Add FPJ As a Trusted Source Dheeraj Kumar Updated: Friday, October 09, 2026, 09:46 AM IST Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary Sets Target Of Making 1 Crore Families Self-Reliant Through Entrepreneurship | X - samrat4bjp Patna: Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Thursday said that the state government fixed the target of helping one crore families become self-reliant through entrepreneurship, focusing on turning the state’s youth into job creators rather than job seekers. After launching the Bihar MSME Policy 2026 and transferring installment amounts to more than 7,000 beneficiaries under the Mukhyamantri Udyami Yojana, Choudhary said the government was working to promote industry, employment and entrepreneurship in the state, adding that the broader objective was to connect one crore families with entrepreneurship. He said that the government aimed at creating an environment where the youth of Bihar became job creators rather than job seekers. CM said 45,000 entrepreneurs were being developed under the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) scheme, for which the state government was spending Rs 3,500 crore. Of the 45,000 beneficiaries, 14,000 would be from scheduled caste and scheduled tribe communities, 10,000 from extremely backward classes, 9,500 women, 9,000 youths and 2,500 from minority communities, he said. ALSO READ Samajwadi Party Chief Akhilesh Yadav Visits Ayodhya, Stays Away From Ram Mandir Choudhary said that under the new policy, 25 to 40 per cent of government procurement would be made from products manufactured in the state. Bihar has set a target of attracting Rs 5 lakh crore in industrial investment through the public-private partnership (PPP) mode and providing 20,000 MW of power to industries over the next five years, he said, and informed that the Centre allocated Rs 10,000 crore for the MSME sector, of which Bihar was expected to receive at least one-tenth. CM also announced plans to construct ropeways at 20 important locations in the state over the next two years and connect all agricultural feeders with 100 per cent solar power within a year. State industries and sports minister Shreyasi Singh, minority welfare minister Zama Khan and senior officials of several departments attended the programme. bihar_raw_news.title: Patna HC Reconsiders Pay Cut and Pension Benefits After 40 Years of Service - Court Book
bihar_raw_news.content: Patna High Court directs Bihar authorities to reconsider a long-serving daily-wage employee’s claims for pay protection, parity and pensionary benefits. Advertisement Join WhatsApp Join Telegram The Patna High Court has directed the competent authorities in Bihar’s Water Resources Department to reconsider the service, pay protection and pensionary claims of a daily-wage employee who worked continuously from 1980 before being absorbed into regular service in 2012. A Single Judge Bench of the Patna High Court, comprising Justice Kumar Manish , was hearing a writ petition filed by the petitioner, who had been working as a daily-wage employee under the Flood Control Circle, Samastipur, since 1980. Advertisement The petitioner, Bipin Kumar Verma, was initially engaged as a daily-wage employee against a sanctioned Class-III Typist post on June 16, 1980. He claimed that several employees who joined after him were regularized between 1984 and 1988, while his case was not considered. He had earlier approached the Patna High Court, which in 1999 directed payment of salary at the minimum of the applicable time scale and later, in 2003, directed the authorities to consider his claim for regularization. After further proceedings, the authorities absorbed him as a Lower Division Clerk through an order dated December 5, 2012. However, the absorption was treated as a fresh appointment, reducing his basic pay from Rs. 9,840 to Rs. 7,730. He therefore sought protection of his earlier pay and recognition of his past service. The petitioner also relied on the cases of other daily-wage employees who, according to him, were similarly placed or junior but had received notional regularization benefits for pension and retirement purposes. He argued that denying him similar treatment was discriminatory. The Court therefore considered whether the petitioner’s past continuous service could be entirely disregarded for pay protection and pensionary benefits, particularly in light of his claim that similarly situated juniors had received notional benefits. The Court also referred to the Supreme Court’s observations in Dharam Singh v. State of U.P. , concerning prolonged engagement of workers under temporary labels and the constitutional responsibilities of the State as an employer. Advertisement The judgment observed: "The petitioner’s long period of engagement and his subsequent superannuation in November 2019 are relevant circumstances, however, entitlement to pay protection and pensionary benefits must be determined separately under the applicable service and pension rules after examining the petitioner’s claim for parity." The Patna High Court directed the competent authority to reconsider the petitioner’s claims concerning the legal effect of his 2012 absorption order, parity with other employees, pay protection under Rule 78 of the Bihar Service Code, and counting of past service for pensionary benefits under the Bihar Pension Rules, 1950. The authority was directed to pass a reasoned order after examining the relevant records and precedents within three months. The writ petition was accordingly allowed to that extent. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar CM directs departments to expedite 'Seva Sankalp, Kayakalp' campaign - ANI News
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar CM directs departments to expedite ‘Seva Sankalp, Kayakalp’ campaign ANI | Updated: Oct 09, 2026 17:00 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Patna (Bihar) [India], October 9 (ANI): Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Friday directed officials of various departments to expedite the implementation of the ‘Seva Sankalp and Kayakalp Abhiyan’ and ensure that the works are completed in a time-bound manner without compromising on quality. Chairing a review meeting with officials of the concerned departments at the ‘Sankalp’ auditorium at Lok Sevak Awas in Patna , the Chief Minister stressed inter-departmental coordination to ensure the effective implementation of the campaign. During the meeting, officials briefed the Chief Minister on the action plan under the campaign through presentations. They also informed him about the construction of new health sub-centre buildings, the arrangement of waiting areas and seating facilities for patients and their attendants, and the establishment of help desks to assist visitors. Choudhary said providing better basic facilities to the public was a priority for the government and directed all departments to work with full commitment, paying particular attention to the quality and timely completion of projects. Reviewing facilities in schools, the Chief Minister directed officials to prioritise painting, construction of boundary walls and repair work. He also stressed ensuring the availability of proper toilets, clean drinking water, electricity and other essential facilities in schools. He instructed officials to construct additional classrooms wherever required and ensure that buildings are constructed for schools that do not have their own buildings, so that students can study in a better environment. He also directed them to expedite the construction of Anganwadi centres. On healthcare infrastructure, Choudhary called for improved facilities at primary health centres, sub-divisional health centres and district health centres to ensure that patients receive the necessary services without inconvenience. He emphasised cleanliness, the availability of essential facilities and the convenience of patients visiting these centres. The Chief Minister also directed officials to focus on the cleanliness and beautification of bus stands, along with ensuring the safety of passengers and the availability of necessary facilities, noting that a large number of people use these facilities for travel. He further instructed officials to promptly restore non-functional streetlights in urban and rural areas and install new lights wherever necessary. He also called for proper maintenance and repair of public tubewells to ensure that they remain fully operational and accessible to the public. The review meeting was attended by Chief Secretary Pratyaya Amrit, Development Commissioner Mihir Kumar Singh, Additional Chief Secretary of the Rural Development Department H.R. national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today stressed the need for young people to continuously upgrade their skills and adapt to emerging technologies amid the rapid pace of technological advancements. He said this while interacting with the representatives of Team India at WorldSkills Competition, Shanghai 2026 at his residence in New Delhi. Congratulating them for representing India on the global stage, Mr Modi urged the participants to develop skills in line with the requirements of the international market and contribute to improving India’s skill training ecosystem through their experiences and suggestions. He also urged them to become ambassadors of skill development. The Prime Minister further emphasised the need for coordinated efforts by youth, the Government and training institutions to establish India as a global hub of skilled human resources. During the interaction, Mr Modi underscored that practical skills are as important as academic degrees. The Prime Minister also underlined the objective behind establishing a separate Ministry for Skill Development and said that the importance of skill training institutions is no less than IITs and IIMs. He encouraged the participants to share their experiences and suggestions with the Government to help improve India’s skill training system. During the interaction, the participants shared their experiences during the competition and expressed pride in representing their country at the world stage. The participants discussed adapting to new tools, software, technical systems and work processes during the international competition. They also spoke about the work being done by the government towards skill development which is helping youth. WorldSkills Shanghai 2026, the 48th WorldSkills Competition, was held from 22 to 27 September 2026 at the National Exhibition and Convention Center in Shanghai, China. Team India secured 10th position at the Competition, winning 6 Silver Medals and 20 Medals for Excellence. Team India was represented by its largest-ever contingent of 70 competitors participating across 63 skills.

national_raw_news.content: The ruling Tamilaga Vetri Kazhagam (TVK) has won the Assembly bypolls for Madurantakam and Dharapuram seats today. In Madurantakam, TVK candidate K Maragatham Kumaravel defeated DMK’s I. Paranthaman by 73,801 votes. The DMK candidate secured 53,743 votes. In Dharapuram, TVK candidate P.Sathyabama won the seat by securing 66,841 votes against DMK candidate S.Suganya who got 57,370 votes with a difference of 9,471 votes. TVK supporters and workers have gathered at the Party headquarters at Panaiyur near Chennai to celebrate the success of their party candidates. The bypolls for these two Assembly seats were necessitated as two AIADMK MLAs resigned from the party and joined the TVK. The election was necessitated as two AIADMK MLAs resigned from their party and joined the TVK . The Dharapuram candidate P.Sathyabama contested the bypoll as a TVK candidate and has won by securing 66,841 votes against DMK candidate S.Suganya with 57,370 votes with a difference of 9471 votes. The Madurantakam TVK candidate K.Maragatham Kumaravel won with 73,801 votes against I.Paranthaman, DMK candidate who secured 53,743 votes with a difference of more than 20,000 votes. The 18 mementoes from Andhra Pradesh featured in the PM Mementoes collection showcase the state's cultural heritage, traditional crafts and public achievements. According to a press release, these gifts, originally presented to the Prime Minister, are now part of a public auction initiative that supports a larger national cause. The collection includes a Kondapalli wooden bullock cart representing rural life and traditional craftsmanship, a Kalamkari textile featuring a photoprint of the Prime Minister, and a commemorative memento from Sree Shivaji Sphoorti Kendram, Srisailam. Together, these items represent the state's folk art, textile traditions and cultural history. As per the release, alongside traditional art and religious craftsmanship, the collection includes mementoes that reflect contemporary priorities and public aspirations. The Stree Shakti Pratibha Award-2025 Commemorative Memento recognises women's achievements, while the Good Governance of India acrylic painting depicts themes such as welfare schemes, agriculture, healthcare, education and infrastructure. Together, these mementoes reflect how gifts from Andhra Pradesh represent not only its cultural identity but also its aspirations for social progress and development, said the release. The PM Mementoes initiative gives these gifts a purpose beyond their original presentation. The mementoes are made available through public auction, and the proceeds are directed towards the Namami Gange programme. Through this initiative, objects that represent Andhra Pradesh's heritage also contribute to a national effort to conserve and rejuvenate the River Ganga, while the cultural significance of the mementoes is preserved. As per the release, the PM Mementoes e-Auction is currently live and has been extended until October 31, 2026. Interested bidders can explore the collection of 18 mementoes from Andhra Pradesh and place their bids on the official PM Mementoes website: https://pmmementos.gov.in. national_raw_news.title: From KYC to patient identity: Why digital trust is becoming critical in healthcare
national_raw_news.content: From KYC to patient identity: Why digital trust is becoming critical in healthcare - Express Healthcare Express Healthcare facebook twitter Email From KYC to patient identity: Why digital trust is becoming critical in healthcare Abhinav Parashar, CEO and Co-Founder, Digio, highlights why healthcare needs to move beyond one-time identity checks to build trust across the patient journey By Abhinav Parashar on October 9, 2026 India’s healthcare system is being rebuilt around digital identity. Health IDs, linked records, teleconsultations, e-prescriptions and online claims are fast becoming the default way patients deal with providers, and a patient is increasingly a login and an ID number instead of a person at a desk. That shift raises a question the sector is only beginning to answer: how does anyone know the person behind the screen is who they say they are? Think about how much of a patient’s care already happens on screens. Appointments are booked on apps, consultations take place over video, prescriptions arrive on phones and reports land in inboxes. The scale is already large. According to the Press Information Bureau (PIB), as of 17 September 2026 India had 97.61 crore ABHA IDs in operation, with 119.95 crore health records linked to them. The same PIB backgrounder reports more than 50 crore teleconsultations, including through the government’s e-Sanjeevani service. Every step assumes the organisation on the other end knows who the patient is. When that assumption is wrong, the damage does not stop at money. A wrong identity can attach the wrong medical record, prescription, diagnosis or insurance claim to a person. Identity is a journey, not a gate Traditional Know Your Customer (KYC) norms in banking treat verification as a checkpoint at the start of a relationship. Healthcare cannot work that way. In a few weeks, one patient may register at a hospital, get tested at a diagnostic lab, buy medicines at a pharmacy, consult a doctor online and file an insurance claim. The cost of getting this wrong is visible in public data. The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG), in Report No. 11 of 2023, audited Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY for the period September 2018 to March 2021. It found that ₹6.97 crore had been paid for the treatment of 3,446 patients who were already shown as deceased in the scheme’s database. The same audit found about 7.5 lakh beneficiaries registered against a single mobile number, 9999999999. The audit pointed to weak validation controls, and recorded the National Health Authority’s response that checks had been put in place. From an identity verification point of view, the lesson is that a record accepted once and never tested against later activity stops being reliable. The real risk sits in the gap between the person, the record and the transaction. A better model is to establish identity once and then recognise the patient reliably at every touchpoint. That means a trusted identity layer sitting beneath registration, consultation, diagnostics, pharmacy, insurance and payments, so patients are not asked to prove themselves again and...

national_raw_news.title: INS Kulish arrives in Singapore as part of Indian Navy's Eastern Fleet deployment
national_raw_news.content: INS Kulish arrives in Singapore as part of Indian Navy's Eastern Fleet deployment Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर INS Kulish arrives in Singapore as part of Indian Navy's Eastern Fleet deployment ANI | Updated: Oct 09, 2026 06:46 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Singapore , October 9 (ANI): Indian Naval Ship Kulish arrived at Tuas Terminal in Singapore on October 6 for operational turnaround (OTR) as part of the Indian Navy's ongoing Eastern Fleet Operational Deployment, aimed at strengthening maritime engagement and regional cooperation. According to an official release, the port call forms part of the Indian Navy's engagement with Singapore and reflects the strong ties between the two countries. The visit provides an opportunity for continued interaction and reinforces the importance accorded to bilateral maritime engagement. During the visit, the Commanding Officer of INS Kulish will call on the High Commissioner of India to Singapore . The officer will also lay a wreath at the Kranji War Memorial, commemorating the historical association between the two countries. The visit is aligned with India's commitment to fostering collective maritime security and promoting regional cooperation. It further contributes to strengthening the shared vision of a safe, secure and inclusive maritime environment, a release added. INS Kulish recently participated alongside the Indian Navy's frontline stealth frigate INS Sahyadri in the 23rd ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting-Plus (ADMM-Plus) Experts' Working Group on Maritime Security Joint Cooperative Activity at Subic Bay in the Philippines. The activity concluded with a closing ceremony on September 25 after a series of coordinated maritime operations aimed at enhancing cooperation and interoperability among participating naval forces. The Indian Navy's participation reaffirmed India's commitment to regional partnerships in line with its Act East Policy and the vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions). Highlighting the engagement, the Indian Navy's spokesperson said in a post on X, "As the ADMM-Plus engagements entered their concluding phase, personnel from #INSSahyadri and #INSKulish undertook cross-deck visits onboard JS Ise and HMAS Perth." The Navy also said that "A Closing Ceremony, marked the completion of the ADMM-Plus #maritimesecurity activities reaffirming the value of professional interactions, mutual understanding and cooperation among the participating maritime forces." Earlier, the Navy said INS Sahyadri and INS Kulish participated in the sea phase of the joint activity alongside maritime forces from participating countries. The operations included Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA), Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR), Maritime Interdiction Operations, Replenishment at Sea, Visit, Board, Search and Seizure (VBSS), Search and Rescue operations and cross-deck landings. The Navy said these coordinated exercises enhanced operational coordination and interoperability through multilateral engagement at sea.
